name: NQuery Quick Info
_comment: Not a language anyone writes. This colorizes the declaration lines the language server puts
in hovers, which NQuery.CodeAnalysis.Symbols.SymbolMarkupBuilder generates in a fixed,
keyword-led shape:
COLUMN CompanyName AS STRING
COLUMN c.CompanyName AS STRING OF TABLE Customers
TABLE Customers
COMMON TABLE EXPRESSION Recent
ALIAS c FOR TABLE Customers
FUNCTION SUBSTRING(text AS STRING, start AS INT32) AS STRING
VARIABLE @x AS INT32
That leading keyword is what makes this possible: source.nquery cannot tell a table name from
a column name, because in a real query both are bare identifiers. Here the preceding keyword
says which is which, so the rules below anchor on it.
The server classified all of this already and Hover flattens it to text (MarkupContent carries
markdown, not classified runs), so these patterns re-derive what was thrown away. If
SymbolMarkupBuilder's wording changes, the affected rule stops matching and its text renders
unstyled -- no error. NQuery.LanguageServer.Tests pins the shapes that matter.
The language is declared in package.json with an empty 'aliases', which keeps it out of the
Change Language Mode picker -- it is not a language anyone opens a file in. That also stops a
```nquery-quickinfo fence in an ordinary Markdown file from picking these rules up, while
hovers still get them. Both are wanted: give this language an alias and it starts colorizing
other people's Markdown and shows up in the picker.

commonTableExpression.comment: Before #table, or the TABLE in 'COMMON TABLE EXPRESSION' would claim EXPRESSION as a name.

column.comment: Both 'COLUMN Name' and the qualified 'COLUMN Table.Name' that column instances produce.

table.comment: 'DERIVED TABLE' has no name after it, so the required identifier keeps this from matching.

type.comment: AppendAsType always writes 'AS <TYPE>', for column, parameter and return types alike.

parameterInSignature.comment: Inside a signature every parameter is '<name> AS <type>'; the type half is taken by #type.

comment: AGGREGATE and the CAST/COALESCE/NULLIF pseudo-signatures name a placeholder with no type
after it -- 'AGGREGATE COUNT(value)' -- so #parameterInSignature, which needs a following
AS, does not reach them. Anchoring on the surrounding '(' or ',' keeps this to positions
that really are arguments. The bracket alternative is COALESCE's '[, ...]'.
Written without look-behind on purpose: Oniguruma rejects the unbounded \s* inside one.

keywords.comment: Whatever the contextual rules above left: DERIVED TABLE, OF, FOR, and the pseudo-signatures for CAST/COALESCE/NULLIF.
keywords.name: keyword.other.nquery
